correctness.rationale: Weyl integration constant-term identity and Clebsch–Gordan yield μ2=1, μ3=1 even (0 odd), μ4=n+1, μ5=T=(5n²+10n+8)/8 even (0 odd), μ6=S=(n+1)(n²+2n+2)/2. Independent coefficient-array Laurent constant-term calculation n2..19 verified all μ2..μ6, independent of package script. Since tensor multiplicities μj are nonnegative, aligned nonnegative coefficients maximize each fixed-magnitude complex pair; even μ3>0 enforces phase alignment when mixed. Odd n>=3 use cubic Bernstein control values 1,5,5(n+1),S, all strictly less than S except final => pure chi_n uniquely optimizes. For even n, Q=P_n(x)/(1+x²)^3, derivative 6H_n/(1+x²)^4; H(0)>0, remaining coefficients nonpositive with strictly negative high terms, so exactly one positive root and K>S. Asymptotics H(c/n)/n²→5/8-c/2 yield x_n=5/(4n)+O(n^-2) and gain 75n/32+O(1). This supports all n analytically; finite moment checks do not establish full maximizer quantifier.
